1/ Introducing Orvena 4B: a 4B model we trained for one job: being the assistant inside Orvena, on the iPhone itself. 
Calendar, alarms, places and travel times, web, and MCP connections like Notion or Linear, often several in one request, in 30 languages. 
Open weights, Apache https://t.co/ItL1psHI0V
Next version of Orvena will ship with Orvena 4B. https://t.co/l2aTghze2g

7/ Weights, bf16 + MTP head, and the technical report: https://t.co/QFPT5TflVs The 4-bit MLX build the app runs: https://t.co/co1VfBrr2j The bench with every model’s results: https://t.co/glHSwx3gTu It’s the default model in Orvena 2.5 for iPhone.

6/ iPhone 17 Pro Max, 14 tasks run twice, median time per task: Orvena 4B: 15.1 s Qwen3.5-4B, thinking off: 16.3 s Qwen3.5-4B, thinking auto (Orvena’s old default): 37.0 s Mostly output length: 169 tokens per turn against 757. Decode is about 21 tok/s, MLX 4-bit.
We also https://t.co/kxJyMxYk2h

5/ The biggest gain is multi-step, 43 of 70 against 17. “Set me an alarm for when I need to leave for tomorrow’s interview, I’m taking the tube” means calendar, location, transit time, then the alarm.
Installed connections don’t distract it. The same 100 everyday requests run https://t.co/xnF23SFFPQ

4/ Results: Orvena 4B: 440 (80.4%) Qwen3.5-4B: 345 (63.1%) Apple on-device: 104 (19.0%)

Apple’s model supports 13 of the 30 languages. In those 13: 84.6%, 67.3% and 29.6%.

- 280B total parameters
- 14B activated per token 
- Pre-trained on 33.5T tokens 
- Up to 1M-token context for fine-tuning and inference 
- FP8 and BF16 weights

Our efficient sparse MoE language model draws on data spanning multiple domains and languages, achieving SOTA on multiple benchmarks among similarly sized base models. Its architecture and training system https://t.co/pksev9jR8j

• Latent-Gated Sparse Attention: concentrates the KV-cache budget on a few full-token layers for long-range retrieval, instead of spreading it thin across many compressed layers.
